observations: Cordless drill with blue and black housing, featuring a 'BOSCH' logo on the side.
The battery pack is labeled '48V' and carries a Bosch logo.
The charger is labeled '48V' and carries a Bosch logo.
The set is housed in a black plastic carrying case with orange latches.
Accessories include a flexible bit extension, various sockets, and driver bits.
A green and white sticker on the inside of the case lid reads 'JANUARY 2022'.
The drill has a keyless chuck and a torque adjustment ring.

claims.evidence: The Bosch logo is clearly visible on the tool, battery, and charger in photo 0.

risks.risk: The item is likely a counterfeit or generic tool; genuine Bosch cordless drills do not use a '48V' battery system in this form factor (standard professional Bosch tools are 12V or 18V).
risks.proof: A clear photo of the manufacturer's specification plate on the side of the drill showing the actual model number and technical specifications.
risks.if_unproven: priced as a generic/unbranded cordless drill

risks.risk: The drill may be non-functional or the batteries may be dead/incapable of holding a charge.
risks.proof: A video showing the drill operating under load and the charger indicator lights functioning when a battery is inserted.

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the specification plate/sticker on the side of the drill body.
Video of the drill running through its speed settings and the LED light (if any) illuminating.
Photo of the labels on the bottom or back of the batteries.
response.reason: The item is identified as a Bosch-branded drill set, but the '48V' specification is a common indicator of a counterfeit product in this market. It is priced as a generic, non-functional tool until proof of authenticity and operation is provided.
